title: Can I SURVIVE 4 Player Chess?
summary: The creator plays chess.com-style Free-For-All 4 Player Chess against three human opponents who are all rated higher than him. Players move clockwise (red, blue, yellow, green) and score points by capturing pieces; checkmate is worth 20 points. Final placement: 1st = 3 wins, 2nd = 1 win, 3rd = 1 loss, 4th = 3 losses. His goal is to place above higher-rated opponents. He plays a cautious 'turtle' strategy, picks off free pieces while others attack each other, and finishes placing above 2000-rated players across games.
rules: Four players (red, blue, yellow, green) on a cross-shaped 14x14 board with 3x3 corners removed, moving clockwise.
Capturing pieces scores points (pawn 1, knight 3, bishop ~5 in FFA ('bishops are worth more'), rook 5, queen 9; a promoted queen is worth only 1 point).
Checkmating a player is worth 20 points; that player is eliminated (their pieces become grey/dead).
Pawns promote on reaching the centre line (crossing the small dark dot in the middle of the board), not the far edge.
A player who is far ahead can claim the win when the others cannot catch up ('They claimed the win').
Clock with increment (~7 seconds added per move).
win_condition: Finish with the most points; placing ranks: 1st 3 wins, 2nd 1 win, 3rd 1 loss, 4th 3 losses. Creator's goal: place higher than the higher-rated opponents.

opponent.name: Three human opponents (rated ~2000-2300)
opponent.avatar_description: Three separate player cards coloured red, yellow and green (default chess.com-style avatars, inferred).

board.shape_notes: Cross/plus-shaped board: 14x14 with 3x3 corners cut out; centre-line promotion marker dot.
board.theme_notes: Thumbnail: purple gradient background with red, green, yellow and blue crowns. Board colours inferred (chess.com 4PC default is grey/white).

setup: Standard 4-player chess setup: each colour has 8 pieces + 8 pawns along one edge of the cross (red bottom, blue left, yellow top, green right).
events: Player elimination on checkmate (pieces go grey)
current_impl_issues: Implemented as 'fourp': a 2-sided 8x8 game where the bot just moves twice per turn - no 4 players, no cross board, no points scoring, no 20-point checkmate, no centre-line promotion, no placement ranking.
